summary: A seat that restarts without a fresh session keeps its held work leases under the new incarnation

replay.detail: No forced replay. The new work.rebound fact projects both incrementally and in a full replay when it is present, and its guards make the projection idempotent.

schema.detail: Registers the work.rebound claim kind (fields, system-only write policy, durable retention) in the claim registry, so the registry digest changes. No table, index, trigger or schema-version change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: Older members retain replicated work.rebound facts as unknown vocabulary pending upgrade, as designed for new claim kinds. Until a member is upgraded, a seat resuming its native session there keeps the previous behavior: its old-incarnation lease is refused and reclaimed. The work action incarnation fence is unchanged; a stale incarnation stays refused.

downtime.detail: Normal binary restart; the rebind runs once per native session report with no additional startup work.

manual.detail: No operator action; existing leases, sessions and identities are preserved.

recovery.detail: Rolling back keeps the durable work.rebound facts as unprojected events; leases replay to the incarnation they recorded before the rebind, which is the previous behavior, with no data loss.
